audits.decision_reason: All critical checks pass. The mechanism specifies a concrete causal path from inter-subject autonomic heterogeneity (HRV, BRS) to residual distribution shifts that violate exchangeability in leave-one-subject-out conformal prediction. Variables are measurable with standard physiological tools, confounders (sensor placement, BMI, medication) are identified and controllable, effect size (>5% coverage deviation for high autonomic variability) is plausible and grounded in literature, data requirements are clear and feasible, and the prediction is testable via correlation of autonomic distance with coverage deviation. The mechanism is domain-specific, invoking autonomic physiology and conformal exchangeability.

All critical checks pass. The mechanism links wearable sensor physics (electrode impedance drift, motion artifacts) to heteroscedastic noise that breaks the i.i.d. assumption for calibration residuals. Variables (impedance, accelerometer variance, SNR) are directly measurable. Confounders (physiological state co-occurrence, sweating, circadian impedance) are identified with control strategies. Effect size (≤80% vs ≥88% coverage) is large but plausible for severe artifacts. Data requirements (wearable data with impedance tracking, ≥100 segments) are clear. The mechanism is specific to wearable sensor non-stationarity and conformal calibration, not generic.

All critical checks pass. The mechanism describes a specific causal path: autonomic state transitions (e.g., sleep stages) cause step-changes in signal dynamics that outpace sliding-window recalibration, leading to coverage drops. Variables (PSG state labels, transition timestamps, residual parameters) are measurable with gold-standard annotations. Confounders (movement artifacts, signal quality, circadian, medication) are identified. Effect size (≥10% drop within 2 minutes) is plausible for fast transitions. Data requirements (PSG-annotated data, ≥50 transitions) are clear. The mechanism is domain-specific, tying autonomic state dynamics to conformal window adaptation.

All critical checks pass. The mechanism specifies how endogenous circadian/ultradian rhythms modulate physiology and SNR, creating periodic residual shifts that fixed calibration windows miss. Variables (DLMO, CBT, cortisol proxies, residual moments) are measurable, with DLMO as gold standard. Confounders (activity, temperature, meals, light) are identified with constant routine as gold-standard control. Effect size (≥5% oscillation amplitude) is plausible. Data requirements (≥48h monitoring, circadian markers, ≥20 subjects) are demanding but clear. The mechanism is non-generic, linking endogenous rhythm biology to conformal calibration periodicity.

All critical checks pass. The mechanism traces how heteroscedastic label noise (inter-rater variability, intra-rater drift) corrupts conformity scores, biasing calibration quantiles. Variables (kappa, noise rate, SQI, conformity scores) are measurable with multi-rater data. Confounders (true ambiguity, SQI, rater fatigue, lab differences) are identified. Effect size (≥8% deviation for kappa<0.7) is plausible for sleep staging. Data requirements (multi-rater annotated data, adjudicated labels) are clear. The mechanism is specific to physiological annotation noise and conformal calibration, not generic label noise.

All critical checks pass. The mechanism links activity context to distinct residual regimes via altered cardiovascular dynamics and sensor noise, causing unstratified calibration to fail. Variables (activity type/intensity, CV dynamics, noise metrics) are measurable with accelerometers and reference hemodynamics. Confounders (motion artifacts, hemodynamic changes, sensor displacement, sweating) are identified with controlled protocols. Effect size (≥15% undercoverage in vigorous activity) is plausible. Data requirements (free-living data, ≥100 segments/stratum, reference BP) are clear. The mechanism is domain-specific, tying activity-induced physiological regimes to conformal stratification needs.

The mechanism is domain-generic. The causal path — unobserved confounders simultaneously influencing signal and target, inducing residual dependencies that marginal conformal coverage does not protect against — applies identically to any prediction problem with hidden confounding (e.g., finance, genomics, climate). It names no physiological-specific process, variable relationship, or boundary condition unique to physiological signals or conformal prediction. The proposed variables (hydration, medication timing) are generic confounders; the boundary conditions (confounders vary systematically, not captured, exchangeability violated conditional on observed covariates) are generic statistical conditions. The mechanism does not explain why this manifests specifically in physiological signal segments or conformal prediction beyond the generic marginal-vs-conditional coverage gap.

All critical checks pass. The mechanism specifies how non-random missingness (MNAR) in wearable wireless transmission creates selection bias in calibration residuals, and how imputation distorts residual distributions differently across segments. Variables (sampling rate, missingness rate/pattern, mechanism classification, imputation method) are measurable. Confounders (physiological state causing both missingness and signal changes, firmware, battery, EMI) are identified. Effect size (MNAR >20% → ≥10% deviation) is plausible. Data requirements (wireless+wired reference, controlled missingness injection) are clear. The mechanism is specific to wearable Bluetooth dropout physics and conformal prediction with imputation.

The mechanism is domain-generic. The causal path — short segment length relative to model complexity causing high-variance empirical quantile estimation, leading to segment-length-dependent coverage instability — is a generic finite-sample property of conformal prediction (or any quantile-based method) that applies to any domain with heterogeneous sample sizes (e.g., NLP with variable-length documents, finance with variable-length windows). It invokes no physiological-specific process; the boundary conditions (event-triggered recordings, model complexity high relative to shortest segments) are generic data-structure conditions. The mechanism does not incorporate any physiological signal property (autocorrelation, non-stationarity, morphology) that would make it specific to physiological signals.

All critical checks pass. The mechanism links model misspecification in waveform-based hemodynamic prediction (e.g., cuffless BP from PPG) to pulse wave morphology features (AIx, PWV, peak ratios) that vary with vascular tone, aging, and pathology. Variables are measurable with tonometry/PPG. Confounders (covariate shift, unmeasured hemodynamics, sensor-specific morphology, dataset shift) are identified with vascular interventions as controls. Effect size (>8% deviation for Wasserstein distance >0.5) is plausible. Data requirements (cuffless BP datasets with reference tonometry, vascular interventions) are clear. The mechanism is highly domain-specific, tying pulse wave morphology physics to conformal coverage failure.
